Our freedoms are not free. They have been defended and preserved by generations of brave Americans who answered the call to serve.
 
North Dakota has a proud tradition of military service. Their service is a real sacrifice for them and their families. Today, we say thank you. An extra big thank you to my father, who served in the Army, and my husband Mike, who served in the Navy.
 
Our service members make sacrifices daily so that we are able to live in freedom and safety. To every veteran and military family across North Dakota and our great nation: thank you for your service, your sacrifice, and the freedoms you've protected for generations of Americans. We are forever grateful. 🇺🇸
 
This Veterans Day, we honor these extraordinary men and women and recommit to keeping the promises we've made to them. They have given so much for our country, and they deserve our unwavering gratitude and support. If you're a veteran who needs help navigating VA benefits or services, please don't hesitate to contact my office or visit my website. We're here to help.

Throwback Thursday songs, tambourines, delicious donuts from Soholt Bakery, and some great questions from 6th and 8th graders at May-Port CG!

What a treat to spend the morning in the classroom with Frannie Tunseth, North Dakota's 2026 Teacher of the Year! Her energy, passion for teaching, and connection with her students make it easy to see why she's earned this recognition!

Thank you, Mrs. Tunseth, for welcoming us into your classroom and for all you do for North Dakota's students!

Yesterday, I visited the LIUNA North Dakota Training Center in Bismarck to learn more about the work they do to prepare folks for careers in construction, energy, and infrastructure.
 
I even had the opportunity to try my hand at holding—not operating—a few different jackhammers! I have a much greater appreciation for the strength and precision operators of these tools need to have.
 
With growing demand for skilled labor across North Dakota, training programs like LIUNA’s are essential to building a strong workforce and supporting our state’s continued growth.

The American Dream is on display right here in North Dakota!

A “hunt” with plenty of wildlife sightings at SilverWing Ranch near Tolley! Tim and Tom Mau took us through the pastures to see their bison and elk up close—a memorable way to experience this unique North Dakota ranch.

Along the way, we learned about their operation and discussed the challenges and opportunities facing our livestock producers. Seeing these impressive animals up close and hearing from the people who raise them made for a great afternoon.

Thank you, Tim and Tom, for the hospitality, the pasture tour, and a wonderful look at the work you do at SilverWing Ranch!

When I took office, I set a goal to go to every county in North Dakota. Yesterday I visited Renville County, completing my visits to all 53 counties!

From the Red River Valley to the Badlands, I’m grateful to the thousands of North Dakotans who have welcomed me into their communities and shared their experiences, concerns, and ideas. 

Every county has its own strengths and challenges. Hearing directly from you helps me and my team identify problems, develop solutions, and serve you effectively in Congress.

I’m pleased to have completed this milestone, and I’ll keep traveling the state and listening to you.

Enjoyed speaking at the Western Dakota Energy Association’s annual meeting in Minot this morning!
North Dakota helps power America, and behind that success are the hardworking people and communities who make it possible.

As energy demand grows, our path forward is clear: https://t.co/f5ZE2WlKmx

Ask any North Dakota farmer and they will tell you: diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) regulations are an expensive daily headache. Today, EPA Region 8 Administrator Cyrus Western joined me in Fargo for a discussion with North Dakota producers, equipment dealers, and manufacturers about how to fix this.

EPA proposals and my DEF legislation would stop “derates.” This is an immediate step to prevent shutdowns and work stoppages. But we need a longer, thoughtful solution that fixes this ongoing and costly problem and provides certainty to all.

Thank you to Titan Machinery for hosting this important conversation and to everyone who took time out of their busy schedules—including harvest—to join us!

Always exciting to be in a room full of talented innovators and researchers!

North Dakota has tremendous opportunities in bioscience, and the research underway at NDSU and Sanford Health to better understand GLP-1 medications and improve obesity treatment is just one promising example.

Enjoyed joining today's BioScience Summit in Fargo and highlighting the research, partnerships, and innovation helping grow North Dakota’s bioscience and biotechnology industries!

Amidon may be North Dakota’s smallest county seat, but the work happening here matters in a big way!

I visited with Slope County Auditor Lorrie Buzalsky at her office to discuss rural elections and the challenges of serving voters across our wide-open spaces. Thank you, Lorrie, and all our local election workers for your dedication to keeping elections secure, accessible, and running smoothly. Every eligible voter deserves to have their voice heard—regardless of where they live.

Creative problem solving is helping keep healthcare close to home in southwestern North Dakota! I visited Southwest Healthcare Services in Bowman to hear how Dennis Goebel and his team are helping people in one of the most remote parts of our state access medical care.

Their participation in the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) supports that work, helping rural providers strengthen services like ambulance coverage, telehealth, and skilled nursing care. It’s an example of how flexible approaches can help meet the unique healthcare needs of rural communities.

Thank you, Dennis and team, for your resourcefulness and dedication to keeping southwestern North Dakota healthy. Rural families deserve care they can count on, and your work makes a difference!

Medical providers are present for some of the most consequential moments in our lives. The care they provide makes a lasting difference for North Dakota families.

🚨 156 Democrats voted against the Laken Riley Act (H.R. 29), which requires federal authorities to detain illegal immigrants arrested for violent crimes rather than release them back into American communities.
🚨 210 Democrats voted against the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act (H.R. 6703), which would help lower costs and increase coverage options.
🚨 197 Democrats voted against the Farm, Food, and National Security Act (H.R. 7567), the first five-year Farm Bill since 2018.
🚨 195 Democrats voted against the SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), which would streamline permitting for American infrastructure projects.
🚨 203 Democrats voted against the Reliable Power Act (H.R. 3616), which prioritizes electric grid reliability.
🚨 107 Democrats voted against the HALT Fentanyl Act (H.R. 27), which gives law enforcement the tools they need to keep deadly fentanyl off our streets.
🚨 206 Democrats voted against the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (H.R. 28), which stops boys from playing in women's and girls' school sports.
🚨 Every House Democrat voted against the SAVE America Act (H.R. 22), which would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
🚨 192 Democrats voted against Condemning and Denouncing Socialism in All Its Forms (H. Res. 1490).
House Democrats are moving full steam ahead in the wrong direction. Their voting record speaks for itself. 🧵

matches.bill_title: Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to modify the Renewable Fuel Standard's definition of "renewable biomass".” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment adds hot rotisserie chicken as an eligible item to be purchased by SNAP benefits.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 20 printed in Part B of House Report 119-628 to mandate a USDA report to Congress (after the SNAP restrictions pilots are completed) on implementation of the restrictions, outcomes, recommendations to Congress.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to repeal and prohibit future implementation of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) rule mandating electronic identification (EID) eartags for bison and cattle moving interstate.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment strikes several sections relating to pesticide labeling requirements.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to preserve greyhound racing operations in West Virginia.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment, as Modified (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment revises the Agriculture Advanced Research and Development Authority program to provide federal support for sustainable agriculture and innovative sustainability solutions.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to add "soda" to the definition of ineligible items and defines soda as a carbonated beverage containing more than 1 gram of added sugar, artificial sweetener, or flavoring per serving.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment removes certain emissions standards on farm equipment.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Recommit — Farm, Food, and National Security Act (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: H.R. 7567 (Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026) reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies Department of Agriculture programs (the farm bill), including commodity support, conservation, nutrition assistance, farm credit, rural development, forestry, and crop insurance. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

roll_calls.question: On Passage — Farm, Food, and National Security Act (H R 7567)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies Department of Agriculture programs (the farm bill), including commodity support, conservation, nutrition assistance, farm credit, rural development, forestry, and crop insurance. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.
